After trading at peaks above $1,600, shares have contracted nearly 60% as investors digest regulatory enforcement from the FHFA and HUD, aggressive competitive price-locking by credit bureaus promoting VantageScore 4.0 at $0.99 through 2028, and a debt-burdened balance sheet loaded with -$5,334M in net debt.

The core investment asymmetry centers on whether FICO's quadruple-digit price increases on mortgage score pulls have permanently exhausted customer goodwill and triggered irreversible disintermediation, or whether secondary mortgage market liquidity will continue to require FICO's predictive algorithms as an immutable standard. While FICO still commands an 83.2% gross margin and an audited Owner ROIC of 71.0%, the market is heavily discounting its ability to sustain 90%+ operating margins in Scores against unified credit bureau pushback and potential bi-merge underwriting transitions.
why_it_might_be_right:
1. Starting Baseline: Starting normalized Owner Earnings stand at $42.99/share ($928.5M total) against a heavily leveraged balance sheet with net cash/debt of -$246.94/share (-$5,334M total debt net of cash) across 21.6M diluted shares.

2. Forensic Business Headwinds: Regulatory intervention via the FHFA credit score modernization initiative mandates the phased adoption of VantageScore 4.0 alongside FICO, while proposed transitions from tri-merge to bi-merge reporting directly threaten to eliminate one-third of all bureau score inquiries. Concurrently, wholesale lenders including Rocket Mortgage and United Wholesale Mortgage (UWM) have begun actively piloting VantageScore to circumvent FICO's $10.00 standard score pricing, while the DOJ continues to scrutinize the company's anti-steering wholesale distribution agreements.

3. Skeptic Unit Contraction: Under this regulatory and competitive disruption, mortgage scoring inquiry volume drops by 25% over the next three years as secondary MBS market guidelines formalize dual-score parity. Concurrently, software segment legacy on-premise runoff accelerates from -8% to -18% annually as enterprise clients reject mandatory cloud migration terms.

4. Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation: Because fixed software hosting costs, regulatory compliance legal overhead, and platform R&D remain rigid, operating leverage turns severely negative. Consolidated gross margin compresses toward 76%, and normalized Owner Earnings contract by 40% to $25.79/share ($557.1M total).

5. Downside Risk Valuation Floor: Capitalizing degraded Owner Earnings of $25.79/share at a trough multiple of 18.0x yields $464.22 per share, and factoring in net balance sheet cash/debt of -$246.94/share results in a Downside Floor Target of $217.28 per share.
how_things_are_going_now:
The operational reality across the trailing four reported quarters reveals extraordinary near-term pricing realization masking underlying volume vulnerabilities. Trailing twelve months revenue stands at $2,393.6M, with latest quarterly revenue of $674.2M establishing an annualized revenue run-rate of $2,696.8M. GAAP gross margin remains elevated at 83.2%, while GAAP operating margin registered at 53.8% (non-GAAP operating margin at 62.0%), underpinned by the Scores division where operating margins consistently exceed 90% due to near-zero marginal distribution costs.

Unit monetization has been characterized by aggressive price extraction. B2B Scores origination revenue expanded rapidly earlier in fiscal 2026 despite muted macro mortgage origination activity, propelled by price increases that lifted benchmark mortgage score royalties toward $10.00. Software segment execution remains bifurcated: Platform ARR grew to $349M (with net retention rates at 136%), but this was substantially offset by non-platform legacy ARR declining 8% YoY to $440M as perpetual maintenance agreements roll off.

Capital allocation has severely depleted the balance sheet. Management funded massive share buybacks using newly issued debt, repurchasing nearly $2.0B of stock in Q3 FY2026 alone. This capital allocation strategy reduced diluted shares to 21.6M but expanded net debt to -$5,334M (-$246.94/share), removing future balance sheet flexibility and eliminating programmatic share repurchases going forward.
what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
1. Starting Unit Baseline: FICO operates from a baseline of ~10.2 billion B2B and B2C credit score inquiries and portfolio reviews, ~28.5 million mortgage origination score pulls (~4.75 million loan files), and ~3.2 billion software platform analytics transactions. Blended unit monetization yields $0.18 across high-volume card/auto inquiries, $10.00 base for mortgage origination scores, and $413M in annualized platform subscription revenue, supporting an annualized revenue run-rate of $2,696.8M.

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Over the next three years, total volume units are modeled to stabilize at a modest 3.0% compound annual growth rate. Platform software expansion and card/auto portfolio monitoring volume offset low-single-digit declines in mortgage inquiries as lenders adopt bi-merge screening on pre-qualifications.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue: Multiplying Year 3 volume units by stabilized unit monetization yield (with mortgage pricing held flat at $10.00 to avoid severe regulatory retaliation) produces Projected Year 3 Revenue of $2,945.7M.

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Deducting cash operating expenses, sales and marketing, R&D, maintenance CapEx of $45.0M, and stock-based compensation of $72.0M from Year 3 Revenue yields Projected Year 3 Total Owner Earnings of $1,053.8M (Owner Cash Margin = 35.8%, or $48.79/share across 21.6M diluted shares).

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Starting Net Cash of -$5,334.0M plus Cumulative 3Y FCF of $2,950.0M minus Cumulative Buybacks of $0.0M (strictly halted due to negative net cash) minus CapEx of $135.0M results in Ending Year 3 Net Cash of -$2,519.0M (-$116.62/share).

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: Projected Year 3 Owner Earnings YoY growth rate moderates to g3 = 4.3% YoY. Selecting the corresponding 2-Factor Exit Multiple of 15.0x P/OE strictly from the Mature Franchise Wide Moat Matrix (3%–8% growth tier) yields:
Year 3 OE $48.79/sh × 15.0x = $731.85 and $731.85 + Ending Net Cash -$116.62/sh = $615.23, resulting in an expected 3-year annualized return (IRR) of -4.97% per annum from today's $717.07 price.
